title: Time Based Key Value Store
statement: Design a store where one key can hold many values over time. set(key, value, timestamp) records a value, and later times for a key are always bigger. get(key, timestamp) returns the value saved at the latest time that is not after the asked time, or an empty string if there is none.

example.caption: foo was set to bar at time 1 and bar2 at time 4. Asking at time 3 gives bar, the newest value that existed by then.

idea.sentence: Keep each key's pairs in the order they arrive. Time only grows, so the list is already sorted, and a binary search finds the latest pair that is not too new.

jargon.plain: You write a small class with methods. The tests replay a list of method calls and compare what each call returns.
Find the largest stored value that is less than or equal to the query, not only an exact match.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the method names and their arguments, e.g. ["TimeMap","set","get"] and [[],["foo","bar",1],["foo",1]]

vars.meaning: number of values stored under one key

compare.bruteLabel: Scan the key's list for get

rows.name: Scan on get
rows.note: Walk the list from the newest end until a timestamp fits. Simple, but slow with many values.

rows.name: Binary search on get
rows.note: The list is sorted by construction, so no sorting step is needed. Space is one pair per set call.

fast.takeaway: Appending in time order keeps the list sorted for free. That buys a fast get without any extra structure.

stages.title: A list per key
stages.note: A map from key to its list of (timestamp, value) pairs. A new key starts with an empty list.

stages.title: set appends
stages.note: Push the pair at the end. Timestamps only grow, so the list stays sorted.

stages.title: get: search range
stages.note: l and r cover the key's list. best starts as an empty string.

stages.title: Candidate or too new
stages.note: Timestamp at most the query: save its value and look right. Otherwise it is too new: look left.

stages.title: Return best
stages.note: The last saved candidate is the newest value not after the query, or an empty string if there was none.

edges.title: Unknown key
edges.why: A missing key has no list. Reading a missing key gives an empty list in both languages, so the loop is skipped and best stays empty.

edges.title: Asked before the first set
edges.why: Every stored time is too new. r walks to -1 and best was never set.

edges.title: Exact timestamp
edges.why: The comparison is <=, not <. A stored time equal to the query is a valid answer.

edges.title: Far in the future
edges.why: The newest pair is the answer. Every middle is a candidate, so l runs off the right end.

gotchas.text: map.get(key) is undefined for a missing key. Use ?? [] before indexing, or list.length throws a TypeError.
Return an empty string, not undefined or null, for no value. Tests compare the result exactly, and null is reserved for methods that return nothing.
Reading a missing map key gives a nil slice, and len(nil) is 0, so no existence check is needed. But do not store through a nil map: Constructor must make the map.
JSON numbers decode into any as float64. The test driver converts them with int(a[2].(float64)). A plain a[2].(int) panics.
Save the candidate and keep searching right (l = m + 1). Stopping at the first fit would return an older value, not the latest one.

recap.pattern: Binary search on a sorted history
recap.key: Append pairs in time order so each key's list is sorted. For get, binary search for the last pair whose time is at most the query.
recap.complexity: set O(1). get O(log n). Space O(total sets).
moves: Map each key to a list of [timestamp, value]
set appends to the key's list
get: if time[m] <= query, save its value and go right. Else go left
Return the saved value, or an empty string
